# Promoted to repo memory: statusline-refresh

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `statusline-refresh M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-08T16:28:59.510Z) — Writing to another initiative with an explicit `initiative` argument TEARS the calling session. sofar_add_note/log_decision/update_task all accept `initiative`, and using one from a session pinned elsewhere lands events where that session is not registered — doctor reports it as "spans N initiatives (torn/leaked)". Observed 2026-08-08: session 9e94756b was registered in drift-certification and peer-messaging, and its notes written with initiative:"writeback-collisions" made it span 3. The explicit argument is for READING another record or for a one-off write you accept the tear for; the clean pattern for real work in a second initiative is a SEPARATE pinned session — sofar_start_session({initiative}) → write → sofar_end_session — which is also what repo-memory M3 already requires for a session working a different initiative than its branch. Corollary for long sessions: re-adopting your own Claude Code session id on each start_session keeps `sofar statusline` accurate, because that line is keyed on the HOST's session id and can only report the home of the registration sharing it; minting fresh ids per work batch freezes the statusline at the first home while the work moves on.
